## Creatine and recovery from critical illness

:::: {.justify}

Many people who survive a stay in intensive care leave
hospital much weaker than before. They can lose a striking
amount of muscle in the first week or two, and for some the
weakness lasts months or years. It affects how well they can
walk, work and look after themselves. There are still no
proven treatments beyond rehabilitation and good nutrition.

Creatine is a natural compound that helps muscles store and
supply energy. As a supplement it is cheap, widely available
and well studied. In healthy adults and older people, adding
it to exercise can modestly improve muscle mass and
strength. Whether that holds after critical illness is
unknown, and the early research is limited and mixed.

We are carrying out a systematic review of all the published
evidence and registered trials of creatine in critical
illness and recovery. We want to find out what is already
known, where the evidence is weakest, and whether creatine
deserves a properly designed clinical trial. In particular,
we are asking when during recovery it is most likely to
help.

::::
